newsitem.title: UK: Russia's oil Co Slavneft plans ADR. [CORRECTED 10:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russia's oil Co Slavneft plans ADR. [CORRECTED 10:50 GMT]

text.p: Russia's fourth largest oil company Slavneft is to undertake an American Depositary Receipt (ADR) issue in the next few months, vice president Andrei Zverev told a conference on Russia.
(Corrects name of company from Slavnest to Slavneft, in headline and text).

In response to as question he said, "As to ADRs we are planning that in the next few months." Fifteen percent of Slavneft is to be sold to foreign investors but Zverev did not say how much would come in ADR form.

Zverev said oil output would rise to 100 million barrels in 1996 from 96.8 million in 1995. "We can achieve this by just re-opening wells which had previously been closed for economic reasons," he said.
Slavneft said it is also planning further processing of its existing wells in Western Siberia. "Three new deposits will be brought into operation," Zverev said.

It will invest another $300 million in upgrading the Mozyr refinery in Belarus, of which $60 million has been guaranteed by U.S. Eximbank and $200 million by Japan's Eximbank. It is also investing $500 million in its Yarolsavinos refinery.
